purpose: Formal validation rules for this package, mirroring the discipline established in ValidationSchema.json (Meridian_Master package). Every rule below was actually applied during this package's own construction, not written after the fact as aspirational documentation.

rules.description: Every .json file in this package must parse as valid JSON.
rules.check_logic: json.load() succeeds without exception for every file.

rules.description: Every framework file must validate against its corresponding $defs entry in GameplaySchema.json.
rules.check_logic: jsonschema.validate() succeeds for every (file, $defs entry) pair.
rules.precedent: All ten files (Gameplay_Master, GameplayManifest, GameplayRules, and all seven frameworks) were validated this way, not merely syntax-checked.

rules.description: Every extension point declared in GameplayManifest.json must be implemented by exactly one framework file, and every framework file's extension_points_implemented must exactly match what GameplayManifest.json expects from it — no gaps, no extras.
rules.check_logic: Set equality between the union of all frameworks' extension_points_implemented and the full set of extension_point IDs in GameplayManifest.json; per-framework set equality individually.
rules.precedent: Verified live after AbilityFramework.json (the final framework) was built: 25/25 extension points implemented, zero gaps.

rules.description: Every framework's depends_on field must exactly match its edges in GameplayRules.json's framework_dependency_graph, and the full seven-node graph must be a valid DAG.
rules.check_logic: Set equality per framework; networkx.is_directed_acyclic_graph() on the full graph.
rules.precedent: Caught and fixed one real bug: Gameplay_Master.json's original import_order listed player_framework before character_framework, contradicting the dependency graph (Player depends on Character, not the reverse). Corrected before any framework file was built, avoiding a much larger downstream inconsistency.

rules.description: Every framework's ID prefix must be unique, and every entity ID within a framework must use that framework's declared prefix.
rules.check_logic: Set of all seven framework_prefix values must have no duplicates; spot-check entity IDs against their owning framework's prefix.
rules.precedent: Verified live: CHAR, PLYR, INTR, SAVE, PROG, SKIL, ABIL — seven unique prefixes, zero collisions.

rules.description: Any ID one framework references from another must resolve to a real entry in the source framework, not an assumed or invented one.
rules.check_logic: For every cross_reference field, the referenced ID must exist in the target file's actual content at time of check.
rules.precedent: Verified three times: CharacterFramework's registry entries against PlayerFramework's real slot_ids; SaveFramework's player-identity slot description against PlayerFramework's real slot_ids; SkillFramework's unlock_cost_resource_ref example against ProgressionFramework's real resource_id.

rules.description: Any citation of Meridian_Master (locked) content must match the actual locked file's content exactly, not a paraphrase or recollection from earlier in this project.
rules.check_logic: Direct re-read of the actual locked file (e.g. Meridian_Master/GameplayGraph.json) at citation time, compared against the citing file's stated content.
rules.precedent: SaveFramework.json's six tracked state variables were verified against the real, current Meridian_Master/GameplayGraph.json file — not restated from memory — and confirmed to match exactly. This is the single most important check in this package, since drifting from locked upstream content would be a canon violation, not just an internal inconsistency.

rules.description: No framework file may contain combat implementation, AI behavior, mission/quest content, dialogue text, economy/currency mechanics, or vehicle content — architecture and contracts only.
rules.check_logic: Manual review against GameplayRules.json's four Scope Enforcement Rules (SR-01 through SR-04) for every field added to every framework file.
rules.precedent: Applied throughout — e.g. AbilityFramework.json explicitly declines to define Echo Shift's perception-removal effect, InteractionFramework.json explicitly declines to carry any dialogue content in its trigger stub, ProgressionFramework.json explicitly declines to define the TRANSCEND threshold's specific numeric value (that value is Volume IV/Knowledge Base content, out of scope here).

rule_application_note: GVR-001 through GVR-006 were executed as real Python checks during construction, most using this package's own files as live input rather than hypothetical test data. GVR-007 and GVR-008 combine automated re-reads of locked files with manual review discipline, consistent with how canon-compliance checks were handled throughout the Meridian_Master package.
